 Judgment

Both the appeal and the cross-objections are arising out of judgment and award dated 01st December, 2022 passed in MVC No.68 of 2022 by the IV Additional District Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-V, Belagavi (for short, hereinafter referred to as the "Tribunal").
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties in this appeal and cross objections are referred to with their status and rank before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the petition are that on 28th November, 2021 at about 4.00 pm when Yellappa was proceeding by walk on the side of road towards Angol Naka on Belagavi-Khanapura Road near Syndicate Bank RPD Cross for selling newspapers, magazines, calendars, etc. at that time, one Hero Honda Splendor Plus motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-24/L- 2914 came from RPD Cross towards Naka being ridden by its rider in a very high speed, rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life without observing traffic rules and thereby lost control the dashed to the said Yallappa from behind and thereby caused the accident.

Due to this impact, Yellappa fell NC:
2023:KHC-D:9023-DB C/W MFA.CROB No. 100036 of 2023 and sustained grievous injuries over the body.

Immediately he was shifted to District Hospital, Belagavi wherein he was admitted as an inpatient from 28th November, 2021 and without responding to the treatment, Yellappa succumbed to the accidental injuries on 10th December, 2021 in the Hospital.
Further, it is stated as to the dependency and also the expenses incurred for rituals and accordingly sought for compensation.
4. In pursuance of notice, respondents 1 and 2 appeared.
Respondent No.1 did not file any statement of objection.

The substance of the statement of objection of Respondent No.2 is that all the legal heirs of the deceased are not impleaded in the claim petition and the petitioners were not depending on the income of the deceased.
The deceased was unmarried and his personal expenses was more than half of his alleged income.
The petitioner No.1 was more than 75 years and hence the age of the petitioner No.1 is to be taken for the purpose of applying the multiplier and not the age of the deceased.
Further it is contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is on higher side and is without any proof.

The rider was riding the motorcycle without wearing NC:
2023:KHC-D:9023-DB C/W MFA.CROB No. 100036 of 2023 helmet and was also not having valid driving licence.
The owner of the motorcycle has entrusted the motorcycle to the rider knowing fully well that the rider was not having driving licence.
The respondent No.1 has not submitted the documents such as policy, Registration Certificate, Fitness Certificate, Driving licence of the rider.
Hence, the liability of the respondent-Insurance Company is subject to the validity and legality of the vehicular documents and also subject to the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
On these grounds sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

8. In view of the above finding, the Tribunal allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.15,32,500/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation from respondents 1 and 2.

Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation and its liability, the NC: 2023:KHC-D:9023-DB C/W MFA.CROB No. 100036 of 2023 Insurance Company has preferred MFA No.100443 of 2023; and being not satisfied with the amount of compensation,
claimants have preferred MFA Crob.100036 of 2023 seeking enhancement of compensation.
9. Heard the learned counsel appearing for parties.
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant-Insurance Company submitted that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is contrary to law and material on record.
It is submitted that the accident occurred only due to negligent act of the deceased.
The Tribunal has wrongly considered the age of the decease as 47 years instead of 60 years as mentioned in Exhibit P3.
Further it is submitted that the Tribunal has wrongly considered the monthly income of the deceased, as the deceased was blind and same is excessive and exorbitant.
On all these grounds sought to allow the appeal.
10. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the claimants submits that the Tribunal has not properly awarded compensation.
The Tribunal has rightly held that the accident occurred only due to rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.

It is the specific case of the petitioners that on 28th November, 2021, deceased Yallappa was walking on the side of the road at Angol Toll-naka for selling newspapers, magazines, etc. and at that time the rider of motorcycle coming in a high speed, rash and negligent manner, dashed against the said Yallappa resultant of which he sustained grievous injuries and later succumbed to the accidental injuries in the hospital.

To substantiate the same, PW1 has reiterated as to the averments made in the claim petition and also produced documents Exhibits P1 to P4 which reveals that on the basis of complaint filed by the complainant, jurisdictional police have registered a case against the rider of the offending motorcycle and submitted First Information Report to the Court.

Thereafter, the Police conducted spot panchnama in presence of panchas, also conducted inquest panchnama, recorded statement of witnesses, obtained post-mortem report and on thorough investigation, Investigating Officer submitted charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle for commission of offence punishable under Section 279 and 304A of Indian Penal Code and Section 134 read with Section 187 of the National Insurance Company Limited vs Smt. The oral evidence of P.W.1 that her son was selling newspapers, magazines and calendars etc.. cannot be doubted.

In the absence of any documentary evidence to show the exact income of deceased, this Tribunal can assess the notional income of deceased based on the avocation and by relying on the schedule of KSLSA.

During the course of cross-examination of PW1, the Insurance Company has not elicited any answer from PW1 to discard the evidence placed by the petitioners.

Considering the oral and documentary evidence placed before it, the Tribunal has held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of motorcycle, which is just and proper and cannot be found fault with.
